title: She Makes $10M/Year and Doesn’t Even Exist (AI Influencers Explained)
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast
promo_conflict: Roma Torres promotes Arcads, his own AI video generation software. He describes its features and customer examples, while many of the revenue and performance figures are estimates or second-hand.

stated_problem.quote: you could build very good static images of AI influencers, but having them talk was very hard.
stated_problem.speaker: Roma Torres

idea.name: Arcads AI video generation software
idea.one_liner: A subscription software platform for creators and advertisers to generate AI actors, scripts, voices, and videos.
idea.customer: Creators, influencers, and companies making ads
idea.offer: Software for generating talking AI actors and ad videos

key_quotes.quote: We really focus on like helping you writing a script selecting an actor
you will get a video of someone who will be talking to the camera with like perfect lip sync emotions.
People are subscribing to our software to create these ads

claims.claim: The platform has a library of thousands of AI actors.
claims.quote: through our library of thousands of existing AI actors

ideas.delivery: Customers use the software to write scripts, select or create AI actors, and generate videos.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR applies to personal data uploaded or generated through the service; consumer subscriptions may trigger DMCC Act requirements.

stated_problem.quote: So, with this new AI short form video generation technology blowing up like crazy, how do you profit from it?
stated_problem.speaker: Chris Koerner

idea.name: AI influencer account
idea.one_liner: Create and grow a virtual influencer account, then earn from sponsored content and brand deals.
idea.customer: Social media audiences and brands seeking sponsored content
idea.offer: AI-generated influencer videos and posts in a focused niche
idea.revenue_model: Brand sponsorships and paid promotional content

key_quotes.quote: create your own AI influencer in a very specific niche
when you get a big enough audience, brands will come and pay you to create content
they only post a couple of weeks and then they give up.

acquisition_channels.details: Post AI-generated influencer content on social platforms to build an audience.
Brands may pay for sponsored posts once the account has a large enough audience.

ideas.delivery: An operator creates an AI persona and publishes its videos and posts on social media; brands pay for promotional content as the account grows.
ideas.other_uk_rules: Paid influencer posts in the UK must be clearly identifiable as advertising under ASA/CAP rules; UK GDPR applies to audience data.

idea.name: Mikuela virtual influencer
idea.one_liner: A virtual influencer publishes sponsored social content for brands, reportedly earning substantial revenue.
idea.offer: Sponsored stories and reels from a virtual influencer

key_quotes.quote: Apparently, she's making $10 million per year in revenue and she doesn't exist.
brands are paying hundreds of thousands to get a a story from her

claims.claim: Mikuela reportedly makes $10 million per year in revenue.
claims.quote: Apparently, she's making $10 million per year in revenue and she doesn't exist.

claims.claim: Brands reportedly pay hundreds of thousands for a story or reel.
claims.quote: brands are paying hundreds of thousands to get a a story from her

acquisition_channels.details: Publish influencer content on social platforms.

ideas.delivery: The virtual influencer publishes sponsored stories or reels; brands pay for placement.

prices: $10 million per year in reported revenue
Hundreds of thousands per story or reel

ideas.other_uk_rules: Paid influencer posts in the UK must be clearly identifiable as advertising under ASA/CAP rules.

idea.name: Alabama admissions TikTok account
idea.one_liner: An AI influencer account posts niche University of Alabama admissions content; no monetization is described.
idea.offer: Admissions-focused TikTok videos from an AI influencer

key_quotes.quote: she created an account for the niche of Walmart.
she created a a profile about like admissions at Alabama.
some of her videos make like hundreds of thousands of views.

claims.claim: Some videos reportedly reached hundreds of thousands of views.
claims.quote: some of her videos make like hundreds of thousands of views.

stated_problem.quote: Everyone who creates content wants to be creating more content.
stated_problem.speaker: Roma Torres

idea.name: AI avatar content service for creators
idea.one_liner: Produce extra social videos for existing creators using their AI avatar, with the creator approving scripts and content.
idea.offer: AI-avatar video production that reduces the creator's time recording to camera
idea.revenue_model: Service fees; the transcript says creators are typically charged less but gives no price

key_quotes.quote: I will create content for you with your avatar and you will validate the the script.
instead of having to record yourself, I'll just like create the content with your avatar for you.
2 million views here 2 million views and all of these videos were created using his AI avatar

claims.claim: Two demonstrated videos each had 2 million views.
claims.quote: 2 million views here 2 million views and all of these videos were created using his AI avatar

acquisition_channels.details: Approach existing influencers and offer to create more content with their avatars; the contact channel is not specified.

ideas.delivery: The service creates scripts and AI-avatar videos for creators, who review and approve the content.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR applies to client likeness, voice, and account data; paid promotions must follow ASA/CAP disclosure rules.

idea.name: AI ad creative agency
idea.one_liner: Create AI-generated video ads for companies already buying ads, charging per package or monthly for creative production.
idea.customer: Companies with active paid advertising, including apps and ecommerce brands
idea.offer: AI-generated ad concepts and videos, with free samples used to win clients
idea.revenue_model: Monthly service packages; the guest suggests $2,000 for 20 ads or $3,000–$5,000 per month

key_quotes.quote: I will create 20 ads a month for you for $2,000.
finding a company that is already spending money on ads and helping them create content.
I will just do that for a 100 companies.
then a third of them will pay for my services and I will sell them the services 3 to 5K per month.
connect to our API through an automation tool like Zapier, Make.com, NA10, Gumloop

claims.claim: A proposed package is 20 ads per month for $2,000.
claims.quote: I will create 20 ads a month for you for $2,000.

claims.claim: The prospects in the example already spend $500,000 per month on Meta ads.
claims.quote: These people will have the budget because they already spend 500k per month on meta ads.

claims.claim: The proposed service could be sold to 100 companies.
claims.quote: I will just do that for 100 companies.

claims.claim: The speaker estimates this approach could reach $20,000 per month.
claims.quote: That's probably the easiest way to get to 20K a month.

claims.claim: A suggested package is 20 ads per month for $2,000, or $100 per ad.
claims.quote: I will create 20 ads a month for you for two $2,000.

claims.claim: The example prospects spend $500,000 per month on Meta ads.
claims.quote: they already spend 500k per months on meta ads.

claims.claim: The $2,000 package is described as less than 1% of the client's ad budget.
claims.quote: So, for them spending 2K is like less than 1% of the ad budget they have.

claims.claim: App companies commonly spend 60% to 70% of monthly revenue on paid ads.
claims.quote: it's a pretty common knowledge that people are spending 70% 60 to 70% of their re monthly revenue in paid ads

claims.claim: The host suggests multiplying app monthly revenue by 0.7 to estimate ad spend.
claims.quote: I've never thought to to do that to take their monthly revenue and just multiply it by.7.

claims.claim: The pitch targets smaller companies rather than firms with more than 200 people.
claims.quote: I would target like smaller company because you don't want to be targeting companies with 200 people plus

claims.claim: The sample compares the service with a UGC ad said to cost $500 and take three weeks.
claims.quote: this UC ad that you probably paid $500 for and that took you three weeks to to get

claims.claim: The first sample ad would be free.
claims.quote: And actually, the first one will be free.

claims.claim: The outreach scenario targets 100 companies.
claims.quote: And I will just do that for a 100 companies.

claims.claim: The speaker estimates 20 to 30 of those companies would take a call.
claims.quote: I will probably get calls like phone calls with 20 30 of them.

claims.claim: The speaker estimates one third of those calls would become paying clients at $3,000 to $5,000 per month.
claims.quote: then a third of them will pay for my services and I will sell them the services 3 to 5K per month.

claims.claim: That scenario would yield $15,000 in revenue.
claims.quote: Yeah, that's already 15K in revenue.

claims.claim: The speaker estimates reaching $15,000 monthly revenue within one month.
claims.quote: In one month I can me be making 15k in revenue doing that with like zero network

claims.claim: An automated workflow could produce 100 to 500 ads per day.
claims.quote: instead of like making one to five a day, I might be doing 100 to 500 a day.

acquisition_channels.details: Find company decision makers on LinkedIn, send a tailored sample ad, and follow up with a pitch.

ideas.delivery: The operator researches active ads, creates AI video ad variations, sends samples, and delivers ongoing creative packages. The guest also describes automating script generation and ad production with an API workflow.

uk_legal_risk.reason: The proposed acquisition method uses unsolicited LinkedIn messages to individual decision makers. Social DMs to individuals or sole traders are restricted under UK PECR; cold email should be limited to corporate subscribers with an opt-out.

ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR applies when collecting and using prospect contact data; provide transparency and respect objections to direct marketing. Paid ads must comply with ASA/CAP rules.

idea.customer: Disability benefit services seeking prospective clients
idea.offer: Qualified leads from people interested in disability benefit assistance

key_quotes.quote: they basically sell leads to these disability companies
they will do the admin work for you to get you this allowance
